definitions.explanation: A literary expression meaning without a name, unknown, or humble. Used to modify nouns and conveys a poetic or elevated tone.

examples.japanese: {名|な}もなき{花|はな}が{咲|さ}いている。
{名|な}もなき{兵士|へいし}たちの{犠牲|ぎせい}を{忘|わす}れてはならない。
examples.english: We must not forget the sacrifices of the unknown soldiers.

examples.japanese: {名|な}もなき{人々|ひとびと}の{日々|ひび}の{努力|どりょく}が{社会|しゃかい}を{支|ささ}えている。
examples.english: The daily efforts of ordinary, unknown people support society.

notes:
A literary or poetic expression meaning "nameless" or "unknown." Composed of {名|な} (name) + も (even/also) + なき (classical negative form of ある, meaning "without"). The classical なき gives it a formal, literary feel.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {名|な}もなき{花|はな}: nameless flowers
- {名|な}もなき{人|ひと}: unknown person; ordinary person
- {名|な}もなき{英雄|えいゆう}: unsung hero
- {名|な}もなき{兵士|へいし}: unknown soldier

REGISTER:
This is a literary expression. In everyday speech, {名前|なまえ}のない or {無名|むめい}の would be used instead. {名|な}もなき appears in literature, poetry, titles of works, and formal rhetoric.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {無名|むめい}: anonymous, unknown — neutral, everyday register
- {名|な}もない: nameless — modern equivalent, less literary
